lens: visual direction: specific, ambitious, drawable silhouette ideas that teach; moods, staging, transitions, teaching machines; kit feasibility
critical: THE FILM'S SPINE IS NOT IN THE KIT, AND staging.kitWork LEAVES IT OUT. 50 of the 122 shots are set in the study and 47 use the narrator's hands, yet docs/film/kit-catalog.md has none of the recurring case devices, and kitWork lists only lanternNetwork, transformerLoom, mistyHills, nightLimb, the reflection compositor and seven small props. Missing pieces, each a blocking dependency: (1) the BELIEF CANDLE per the CANDLE-CLOCK RULE: 45 scored rings at 6 px, a ghost sleeve, live / out-with-smoke / frayed states and a base tag. The kit's candle() and candlestick({burn}) are brass candlesticks with no rings or sleeve, and this candle is used in about 25 shots plus the finale's wax bar chart. (2) candleShelf, the CASE BOARD (slot grid K, S1–S3, C1–C4, F1–F2, Q1–Q4, with cards, brass pins, threads of light and the oxblood thread), the WALL OF FORECASTS (W1–W8) and the X-RAY COLUMN (seven bands plus the seam). (3) A narrator-hands FOREARM RIG with its six actions. puppet/hands.ts offers only the props pipe, chalk, pen, book, clipboard, papers, mug, laptop, phone and cards: no match, brass pin, rubber stamp, manila file or fountain-pen writing. (4) threadsOfLight and attentionMath are hard-wired to 'The animal didn't cross the street…', but ch10-s04, ch10-s06, ch10-s07 and ch10-s08 need {tokens, weights[h][i][j], cups:n, etched shares} overrides. (5) alexnetCathedral has no 96-tile filter mosaic (noise→learned, ch08-s06), no 48/48 colour-agnostic/colour-specific sort (ch08-s09) and no rose-window layer vignettes (ch08-s05). (6) sets/hallOfMirrors with reflected, head-turning audiences (ch05-s01, ch15-s01). (7) A paper globe of lit windows (ch07-s03, ch07-s04, ch15-s07); the kit globe() is a desk globe. (8) Symbolic animal cut-outs: frog (ch02-s08), octopus, bear and parrot (ch11-s08), gopher and chinchilla (ch11-s07); also stopwatches (ch15-s04) and courthouses and gavels (ch15-s05). FIX: add all of these to staging.kitWork as blocking items with their shot lists. For (1)–(3), specify ONE derived state table, boardStateAt(shotId) / shelfStateAt(shotId) / wallStateAt(shotId) / xrayBandsAt(shotId), generated from staging.caseBoard.slots, candleClock.candles and wallOfForecasts. That way every study shot renders the same board, shelf and Wall for its moment in time, instead of 50 authors re-deriving which cards, rings and slips exist. For (5), if real conv1 weights are not used, tag the mosaic ILLUSTRATIVE.

RUNTIME IS FURTHER OVER THAN IN ROUND 3. 3,638 spoken words (target about 3,040). Summing leadIn, words, pauses and holdAfter (with minDuration floors) gives 36.5 min at 2.5 words/s, 38.5 at 2.3 and 42.4 at 2.0. The target is 32 min and the brief's maximum is 35. Several fixes below, which make on-screen payloads fit, add hold time. FIX (visual lens, where the picture already teaches): (a) cut about 450 words, starting with lines the image already carries: ch14-s07 L1421 (the three tags are the voices); ch15-s05 L1525 down to about 12 words (the terrarium, valve and building carry the method); ch05-s04 L0520 (the family-tree tints carry it; keep one clause); ch09-s03 L0906's 'which it reckoned a human would choose once in ten thousand' (the '1 in 10,000' stamp carries it); ch08-s13 L0825 (the IDSIA inset carries it); ch12-s08 is already lean. (b) Of the 15 lampChanges (each about 3 s, through black), keep only true act breaks (ch01-s04, ch05-s01, ch13-s01, ch15-s08). Turn every other return to the study (ch02-s08, ch05-s06, ch06-s07, ch08-s13b, ch10-s13b, ch13-s06) into a reverse FLAME PUSH, pulling out of the stage candle's flame onto the shelf with crossfadeMood. That saves about 1.5 s each and keeps the film out of black. ch02-s06, ch04-s03, ch10-s04, ch11-s08 and ch12-s06 can become crossfades with crossfadeMood. (c) Trim payloads, not holds, wherever this card offers the choice.

TIMING FIELDS CONTRADICT THE PAYLOADS THEIR OWN VISUALS PROMISE. set 5.5. ch07-s06: holdAfter 4.2 has to carry the 2 s coat tie, the 4.5 s X-ray and two clue pins with a thread; set 9, or move the C3 pins into ch07-s04's hold. ch08-s13b: 'about 8.5 seconds' against holdAfter 7, which includes the desk-lamp click; set 9. ch10-s03: Kelcey's card is 'about 6 seconds' against holdAfter 3.9 (about 100 characters needs about 9.8 s); cut to '…the biggest incorrect prediction of my life' and set 5.5. ch10-s10: 'about 7 seconds' against holdAfter 3.6; set 6.5 or cut the caption to 'untrained toy weights: real bindings' (about 36 characters, 4.5 s). ch10-s14: holdAfter 2.5 has to carry the crossfade, a 4.5 s X-ray, the C3-d pin and a thread; set 7.5. ch11-s01: 'at least 15 seconds' against minDuration 12; set 15 or cut the walking machines to one pass. ch11-s03: the temperature dial is placed 'in the long hold' but the X-ray is anchored on 'No rulebook' mid-line, before the hold, and the hold is only 3.3 s; move the dial into a raised pauseAfter on L1105 (about 3.5 s) and keep the X-ray reveal in a 5 s hold. ch11-s08: 'about 8 seconds' for Marcus against a pause of 4.22; set the pause to 5.5 (46 characters). ch13-s06: leadIn 2.4 has to include the lampChange (at least 1.6) plus the Cyc candle going out and its 22-character tag; Its 95-character microscope quote also gets a 5.5 s hold; cut it to '…satisfying insight for about a quarter of the prompts…' or set 8.5.

strengths: The teaching machines are still the film's glory, and every one is bound to real numbers a shot author can render. The perceptron knobs turn only on mistakes (ch03-s04). The scissors cannot cut XOR, then two cuts and a fold can (ch04-s01). The messenger bead tugs each string by its gradient (ch05-s04). The 3.88 stencil cell has all nine terms shown (ch08-s04). The jug pours a real softmax (0.20 · 0.07 · 0.53 · 0.20, ch10-s06), and √d is taught by the jug slamming into one cup and frosting over (8 · 0 · −8 → 1.00 · 0.00 · 0.00 against 0.67 · 0.24 · 0.09, which I checked, ch10-s07). The typesetter's case uses the kit's real NEXT_TOKEN_DEMO shares with a temperature dial (ch11-s03).

Most round-3 criticals landed cleanly. The founding grammar is now one object set for both labs (bare pins, a warm/cold lantern pair, one ledger). Chapter 14 has a WINDOW RULE with mullions as the L1 occluder, a single-plane 35% reflection and a push through the glass to open, and no red on the strait. kitWork exists. The X-ray payoff has a 10 s lead-in at 1.1 s per band with a chime each. The stampede montage has 2–4-word captions at 2.2 s spacing. The shelf in the finale runs strictly by year lit, with the still-lit flames scattered across it.

The recurring grammar does real story work in pictures. Believers stand in the light and doubters at the rim. Hinton's walk runs seated at the rim (1976), then standing at the centre (2012), then back at the rim (2023), with a ghost of his younger self (ch13-s02). Three overlapping lamps replace 'two teams' (ch13-s04). The Hall of Mirrors turns away in 1981 and turns back for the Nobel (ch05-s01 / ch15-s01). The rewind plays forward into the chat box. A hand from the viewer's side lights an unlettered candle (ch15-s09).

Fairness is drawn, not just stated. The two shores are mirror-balanced with the same palette and window rhythm and no emblems. Two identical shuttered and open windows for o1 and R1 (ch15-s02). Identical lab lamps with equal time per stop (ch15-s05). Two equal 'accounts' cards for Gebru's exit (ch11-s08). The Go makers get their own cool practical rather than the doubters' rim (ch09-s03).

Restraint is used where it matters. The deaths of Pitts and McCulloch are told by two lamps on sills (ch04-s04). Rosenblatt's death is a single candle and the dedication (ch04-s05). The Nobel night shows an empty hotel room (ch15-s01). Widrow's Dartmouth lantern is still lit on the sill (ch15-s07), and the MTurk globe goes dark window by window. These are the moments a viewer will remember.
